newsitem.title: European Union: Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary for May 5-Dec 31, 1997 (page 1/6 - May 5-17).
newsitem.headline: Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary for May 5-Dec 31, 1997 (page 1/6 - May 5-17).

text.p: **** HIGHLIGHTS **** AMSTERDAM - The Netherlands hosts summit of European Union leaders (June 16-17). MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9). LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg hosts summit of European Union leaders (December 12-13). BRUSSELS - Conference of Bosnian donor countries originally scheduled for April has been POSTPONED to an unspecified date before June. MONDAY, MAY 5 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Finnish Prime Minister Pavo Liipponen meets European Commission President Santer and Commissioner de Silguy; discussions to cover state of the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms, economic and monetary union, EU enlargement and the EU's northern dimension. BRUSSELS - The Euro Citizen Action Service (ECAS) holds conference on "Preparing Citizens' Europe Day" (0900/0700 GMT) (To May 6). Venue: European Parliament, Van Maerlandt II. Contact: Jessica Erba (322) 548 0499. INNSBRUCK, Austria - EU Committee of the Regions holds seminar on "Transport policy for sensitive areas". Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155. TUESDAY, MAY 6 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting. Provisional agenda includes proposal for rules on airport slots, reports and proposals on EU fight against fraud and corruption, report on climate change. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Institute for Asian Studies holds lunchtime meeting on "The Burmese economy and the GSP case" covering the EU's Generalised System of Preferences trade scheme (1230/1030 GMT). Venue: European Institute for Asian Studies, 35 rue des Deux Eglises. Contact: Zoe McCarthy, European Insitute for Asian Studies (322) 230 8122. LUXEMBOURG - NATO and Russia hold a new round of talks in an attempt to strike a deal on a new post-Cold War pact. NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov attend. WEDNESDAY, MAY 7 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament Subcommittee on Monetary Affairs meets (0930/0730 GMT). BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) Secretary General Emilio Gabaglio holds news conference to present ETUC's views on the Amsterdam EU summit and its plans for a "Tour for jobs" cycle ride (1030/0830 GMT). Venue: ETUC headquarters, Auditorium 155 Blvd Emile Jacqmain. Contact: ETUC (322) 224 0411. THURSDAY, MAY 8 - EU institutions closed for Ascension holiday. FRIDAY, MAY 9 - EU institutions closed for "Robert Schuman" remembrance day. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Final session of the inter-governmental conference (IGC) for young people, a simulation of EU treaty reform talks by pupils at Brussels schools. Venue: European Parliament, Leopold building. SATURDAY, MAY 10 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Open house at European Union buildings. BRUSSELS - European Association of Lawyers for Democracy and World Human Rights (EALDH) holds conference on "Environmental law in Europe" (1300/1100 GMT). Venue: German Land Hessen Representation to the EU. MONDAY, MAY 12 BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes annual EU excessive deficit review, to see which countries have deficits and debt out of line with the Maastricht treaty. BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To May 13). No agenda yet available. STRASBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds plenary session (To May 16). Provisional agenda includes debates on a code of conduct for EU lobbyists; EU energy and environment policies; trans-European telecommunications networks; EU rules on public contracts; marketing rules for weedkillers, pesticides and other "biocides"; European defence industries; regional cooperation between the countries of ex-Yugoslavia; ratification of the UN Law of the Sea Convention implementation agreement. PARIS - Western European Union ministers meet (To May 13). LONDON - IBC UK Conferences Ltd. holds conference on "EC competition law" (To May 13). Topics include: the green paper on vertical restraints and exhaustion of intellectual property rights. Venue: The Hyde Park Hotel. Contact: IBC UK Conferences Ltd. (44) 171 453 2711. MUNICH - European Air Law Association holds seminar on "Liability claims handling in the airlines and aerospace industries" (1915/1715 GMT). Venue: Kempinski Hotel Airport. Contact: European Air Law Association (49) 89 365 061. TUESDAY, MAY 13 HABAY-LA-NEUVE, Belgium - European Commissioner Van Miert addresses Arlon Committee Financial Forum on "Competition: European stakes and perspectives" (1130/0930 GMT). Venue: Salle d'Anlier. Contact: Arlon Committee Financial Forum (32) 63 22 39 87. LONDON - The European Regions Airline Association (ERA) holds third annual crisis management conference (To May 14). Discussions will focus on the examination of every element of disaster planning, from the immediate response to longterm considerations. Venue: Ramada Hotel, Heathrow Airport. Contact: ERA (44) 276 856495. WEDNESDAY, MAY 14 BRUSSELS - EU research ministers meet (To May 15). Provisional agenda includes preparation for discussions with Central and East European ministers, additional financing for the research Fourth Framework Programme, the Fifth Framework Programme, international cooperation on science and technology. FLORENCE, Italy - European Natural Gas Vehicle Association (ENGVA) holds conference on "Creating the climate for NGVs" (To May 16). Contact: ENGVA (31) 20 597 3100. THURSDAY, MAY 15 BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts round table on practical aspects of the passage to the euro. Participants include representatives of consumer assocations, small and medium-sized enterprises, banks, unions, national and local administrations. BRUGES, Belgium - European grain lobby COCERAL holds congress to celebrate its 40th anniversary (To May 15). Contact: Chantal Fauth (322) 502 0808. AMSTERDAM - EU Committee of the Regions holds first summit of the regions and cities (1600/1400 GMT) (To May 16). Discussions focus on structural funds, enlargement, employment, inter-governmental conference. Speakers include: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, European Commission President Jacques Santer, European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles, Committee of the Regions President Pasqual Maragall. Opening news conference at 1530/1330 GMT; closing news conference on Friday at 1800/1600 GMT. Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155. SATURDAY, MAY 17 GENEVA - The International Telecommunications Union celebrates World Telecommunications Day - "Telecommunications and humanitarian assistance", commemorating its founding in Paris 132 years ago. Contact: International Telecommunications Union (41) 22 730 5111. 291321 DED:BC-DIARY-LONGTERM =2 Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 2/6 - May 19-June 2) MONDAY, MAY 19 - EU institutions closed for Whit Monday holiday. TUESDAY, MAY 20 BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To May 21). No agenda yet available. BRUSSELS - EU internal market ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes impact and effectiveness of the internal market, legislative simplification, legal protection of designs, precious metals, in vitro diagnostic equipment, masses and dimensions of certain motor vehicles, programme to improve awareness of legal professions of EU law, supervision of insurance companies, safety standards of buses and rules for making foods including sugar, honey, fruit juices and coffee extracts. PARIS (NEW ITEM) - European Association of Securities Dealers (EASD) holds conference on "The new European stock market for growing companies" (0900/0700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Royal Monceau. Contact: EASD (322) 227 6565. WEDNESDAY, MAY 21 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Road Safety Federation (ERSF) holds news conference to launch its five-year medium-term programme on nonlegislative activities for road safety in the EU in the context of the communication on road safety recently adopted by the European Commission (1315/1115 GMT). Venue: Swissotel. Contact: Sandrine Poelmans, ERSF (322) 282 0828. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Belgian Association for Environment Rights holds conference on "Citizens and association rights in European environmental law" (0845/0645 GMT). Venue: SAS Radisson Hotel. Contact: Belgian Association for Environment Rights (32) 9 264 6926. BRUSSELS - World Fuels Conferences holds conference on "Fuel quality and vehicle technology" (To May 23). Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: World Fuels Conferences (1) 703 812 0902. THURSDAY, MAY 22 BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds conference on "A time for change: the effect of the euro on new and existing stock exchanges and the presentation of the AIM (Alternative Investment Market)" (1400/1200 GMT). Venue: Auditorium Societe General, 30 rue Royale. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium fax (322) 512 8363. FRIDAY, MAY 23 - (possibly) EU member states hold extraordinary summit to give an extra push to efforts to seal a new treaty for the Union (location not yet announced). BRUSSELS - European Institute of Public Affairs and Lobbying (EIPAL) holds conference on "Practice and legal restrictions on lobbying the European institutions" (1400/1200 GMT). Venue: EP. Contact: Glacomo Scuart, EIPAL (322) 481 7325. SUNDAY, MAY 25 MIDDELBURG, Netherlands - EU agriculture ministers hold informal meeting (To May 27). No agenda yet available. FRANCE - French parliamentary elections. MONDAY, MAY 26 BRUSSELS - EU energy ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes liberalisation of gas market, EU strategy on renewable energy and Energy Charter Treaty. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Academy of European Law Trier (ERA) holds conference on "Should we establish European environment mediators in the member states?" (0900/0700 GMT) (To May 27). Venue: Borschette Centre. Contact: ERA (49) 651 147100. TUESDAY, MAY 27 BRUSSELS - EU justice and home affairs ministers meet (To May 28). Provisional agenda includes examination of the UNHCR repatriation plan for Bosnians, organised crime, drugs, trafficking in human beings and sexual exploitation of children, money laundering, Europol police agency, customs cooperation, asylum seekers, terrorism, racism and xenophobia, draft convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters, draft convention on corruption involving EU officials. BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds conference on "EU climate change targets: the impact on business" (0900/0700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Bristol Stephanie. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium fax (322) 512 8363. BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) gives Bentick prize award to Former Portuguese President Mario Soares for his role in European integration and his struggle against dictatorship. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911. BRUSSELS - Institute for International Research (IIR) holds "Euro III" conference on the practical consequences of the single currency on information technology, accounting and taxation (0900/0700 GMT) (To May 28). Venue: Sheraton Brussels Airport. Contact: IIR (322) 776 0400. WEDNESDAY, MAY 28 BRUSSELS - European Parliament holds mini session (To May 29). BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - (possibly) European Parliament and Council start conciliation procedure to iron out differences over ARIANE and RAPHAEL cultural programmes. BRUSSELS - EU Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To May 29). THE HAGUE - U.S. President Bill Clinton and EU Dutch Presidency hold bi-annual summit (To May 29). Main discussions focus on European security, the Middle East, situation in former Yugoslavia and Russia; Clinton is also expected to attend commemoration of 50th anniversary of U.S. Marshall plan for post-war reconstruction of Europe. SCHEVENINGEN, Netherlands - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Cost/Benefits of health/safety at work" (To May 30). THURSDAY, MAY 29 BRUSSELS (MODIFIED ITEM) - EU telecoms ministers meeting has been POSTPONED to unspecified date in June. BRUSSELS - (Possibly) EU transport ministers meet to finalise transport accord with Switzerland. LISBON - NATO foreign ministers hold informal meeting (To May 30). Discussions focus on NATO enlargement and reform; agreement with Russia and enhanced Partnership for Peace programme; preparations for NATO summit in June. THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts seminar on "Good governance for Central and Eastern European Countries" (To May 30). PARIS - CICERO Foundation holds conference on "Results of the IGC - Preparing the Amsterdam Treaty". Main topics discussed - the issue of flexibility: will Britain block "Core Europe"?; the special strategy of the Dutch presidency; reforming Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP); the chances for a Mr CFSP; a breakthrough in the third pillar (Justice and Home Affairs)?; institutional arrangements; power struggle or compromise; the IGC seen from Central and Eastern Europe. Contact: CICERO Foundation (33) 1 43 80 18 21. FRIDAY, MAY 30 GENEVA (NEW ITEM) - Cameron May Conferences holds second annual conference on "Dispute resolution in the World Trade Organisation" (0900/0700 GMT). Agenda includes: current status of WTO dispute settlement; contributions of the appellate body to rule of law; the role of economics in WTO dispute settlement; the private sector view of WTO dispute settlement; new aspects to the EU approach to the dispute settlement system - Trade barriers regulation. Venue: The Intercontinental Hotel. Contact: Cameron May Conferences (44) 171 582 7567. SUNDAY, JUNE 1 FRANCE - French parliamentary elections. MONDAY, JUNE 2 LUXEMBOURG - EU foreign ministers meet (To June 3). Provisional agenda includes signature of agreements with Egypt, Lebanon and Jordan; preparation for the Amsterdam EU summit; discussions on former Yugoslavia, the Middle East peace process, association agreement with Algeria, partnership and cooperation agreement with Ukraine, Nigeria, transatlantic relations. 291342 DED:BC-DIARY-LONGTERM =3 Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 3/6 - June 3-26) TUESDAY, JUNE 3 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - CEO Summit Conference on Converging Technologies (To June 4). Speakers include: European Commissioners Mario Monti, Emma Bonino, Marcelino Oreja, Karel Van Miert; U.S. Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt; British Science and Technology Minister Ian Taylor; Microsoft Europe President Bernard Vergnes; Apple Computer CEO Gilbert Amelio; France Telecom President Michel Bon. Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: (1) 216 479 8420. THURSDAY, JUNE 5 LUXEMBOURG - EU health ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes EU health monitoring and epidemiological surveillance; programmes on pollution-related diseases, injuries and rare diseases; ways to reduce smoking, organ transplants, drug dependence, EU-U.S. task force on global early-warning system for communicable diseases and "mad cow" related diseases in humans. LUXEMBOURG - EU development ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes future EU relations with African, Caribbean and Pacific countries; human rights/good governance; forestry policies and research policies in developing countries. THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts K4 Committee (consisting of officials from interior ministeries of EU member states) meeting (To June 6). No agenda available yet. SUNDAY, JUNE 8 NOORDWIJK, The Netherlands - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Regional planning and regional policy" (To June 10). MONDAY, JUNE 9 LUXEMBOURG - EU agriculture ministers meeting has been POSTPONED to June 16-17. LUXEMBOURG - EU finance ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes preparation for the Amsterdam EU summit, preparations for introduction of the single currency, implementation of 1996 economic policy guidelines and draft guidelines for 1997, employment, fight against fraud. STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To June 13). TUESDAY, JUNE 10 BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0800 GMT). LONDON - Agra Europe holds first European cheese conference (To June 11). Venue: The Waldorf Meridien Hotel. Contact: Agra Europe (44) 1892 511807. WEDNESDAY, JUNE 11 BRUSSELS - EU Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (To June 12). THURSDAY, JUNE 12 LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes employment policy, burden of proof in sex discrimination cases, worker consultation, collective redundancies, part-time jobs, home working. MILAN, Italy - Euromanagement holds conference on "Managing the future growth of cogeneration in Europe" (To June 13). Contact: Euromanagement (31) 40 2974 944. MONDAY, JUNE 16 LUXEMBOURG - EU agriculture ministers meet (To June 17). No agenda available yet. AMSTERDAM - Dutch presidency hosts European Council of heads of state or government (To June 17). Provisional agenda includes presentation of a report on organised crime, completion of the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms, legal framework for introducing the euro single currency, European Commission action plan and timetable for removing remaining internal trade barriers by the time the euro is introduced. TUESDAY, JUNE 17 LUXEMBOURG - EU transport ministers meet (To June 18). Provisional agenda includes air transport noise, air transport negotiations with the United States and Central and East European countries, EU membership in the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation, proposed European organisation responsible for civil aviation safety, charges on heavy goods vehicles, seafarer training, sea passenger registration, transport negotiations with Switzerland. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Food Law sixth annual conference (To June 17). Main issues discussed are food safety; genetically modified foods and food law. Speakers include: MEPs Roth-Behrendt and Collins. Venue: Radisson Hotel. Contact: IBC (44) 1892 511 807. THURSDAY, JUNE 19 LUXEMBOURG - EU environment ministers meet (To June 20). Provisional agenda includes climate change, control of car emissions, acidification, biological diversity, petrol and diesel fuel quality, water quality, waste landfills, waste shipments. FRIDAY, JUNE 20 DENVER, United States - Group of Seven (Britain, U.S., Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan) hold summit (To June 22). MONDAY, JUNE 23 LUXEMBOURG - EU fisheries minsters meet. Provisional agenda includes fish capacical measures, fishing management in the Baltic Sea, herring fishing for purposes other than human consumption; ratification of British agreement on straddling stocks. LUXEMBOURG - EU finance ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes follow-up to the EU Amsterdam summit, preparation for introduction of the single currency, adoption of 1997 economic policy guidelines. HELSINKI - International Union of Railways hold third Pan-European transport conference (To March 25). Contact: International Union of Railways (33) 1 44 49 20 50. WEDNESDAY, JUNE 25 BRUSSELS - European Parliament hoJune 26). AMSTERDAM - The Netherlands Industrial and Agricultural Biotechnology (NIAB) Foundation holds "EuropaBio '97" (To June 27). Speakers include: European Commissioner Brittan, Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers. Venue: RAI Congress Centre. Contact: Lidy Groot Congress Events (31) 20 679 3218. THURSDAY, JUNE 26 LUXEMBOURG - EU foreign ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes signature of cooperation agreements with Albania, Yemen and Andorra; signature of partnership and cooperation agreement with Turkmenistan; follow-up to the EU Amsterdam summit; former Yugoslavia and the Middle East peace process. LUXEMBOURG - EU education ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes European Commission reports on education and training, mobility in higher education, learning in the "information society". LONDON (NEW ITEM) - Congress on "Digital television - Economics, regulation and strategy" (To June 27). Venue: Le Meridien. Contact: Fiona Walker (44) 171 421 3500. NORROEPING, Sweden - EU Committee of the Regions holds seminar on "Transport problems in the Baltic area". Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155. 291347 DED:BC-DIARY-LONGTERM =4 Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 4/6 - June 27-Oct 13) FRIDAY, JUNE 27 AMSTERDAM - EU will brief central and eastern European countries on the outcome of the EU Amsterdam summit. MONDAY, JUNE 30 LUXEMBOURG - EU culture ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes amendments to the "television without frontiers" directive on cross-border broadcasting, proposed fund for EU audiovisual producers, cooperation between public broadcast corporations, decision on European Cultural Cities. * Dutch EU presidency ends. Luxembourg takes over to December 31, 1997. THURSDAY, JULY 3 LUXEMBOURG - European Commission on official visit to Luxembourg. MONDAY, JULY 7 BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet and hold structured dialogue with Central and East European countries. TUESDAY, JULY 8 MADRID - NATO holds summit to chart course for enlargement and invite a number of former communist foes to begin membership talks (To July 9). (possibly) In margins of the summit, EU Luxembourg presidency, European Commission and U.S. meet to discuss trans-Atlantic issues. WEDNESDAY, JULY 9 BRUSSELS - EU Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To July 10). THURSDAY, JULY 10 EDINBURGH - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds conference on "Network industries in Europe: preparing for competition" (To July 11). Speakers include: European Commissioner Neil Kinnock. Venue: Balmoral Hotel. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911. SATURDAY, JULY 12 LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers hold informal meeting (To July 13). No agenda yet available. MONDAY, JULY 14 STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (to July 18). WEDNESDAY, JULY 16 STRASBOURG - (possibly) European Commission gives opinions on EU membership applications of Eastern European countries. STRASBOURG - Luxembourg EU presidency presents work programme to the European Parliament. MONDAY, JULY 21 - EU institutions closed for Belgian Independence Day holiday. TUESDAY, JULY 22 BRUSSELS - EU foreign ministers meet (To July 23). No agenda yet available. BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To July 23). No agenda yet available. THURSDAY, JULY 24 BRUSSELS - EU budget minsters meet. No agenda yet available. AUGUST - EU institutions closed for summer holidays. SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 7 ECHTERNACH, Luxembourg - EU agriculture ministers hold informal meeting (To September 9). No agenda yet available. FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 12 MONDORF, Luxembourg - EU finance ministers hold informal meeting (To September 14). No agenda yet available. MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 15 BRUSSELS - EU foreign ministers meet (To September 16). No agenda yet available. STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To September 19). WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 17 BRUSSELS - EU Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (To September 18). FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 19 BANGKOK - European and Asian finance ministers meet under the Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM) framework. MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 22 BRUSSELS - EU justice and home affairs ministers meet (To September 23). No agenda yet available. BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To September 23). No agenda yet available. THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 25 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - International Centre of Research and Information on the Public and Cooperative Economy (CIRIEC) holds conference on "The public, social and cooperative economy and the general interest - Which roles in the 21st century?" (0830/0630 GMT) (To September 26). Speakers include European Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies. Venue: Palais des Congres. Contact: CIRIEC (322) 366 2746. SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 27 TOKYO - Asian and European economy ministers meet under the Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM) framework. (To September 29). OCTOBER LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg EU Presidency hosts high-level meeting in the framework of preparations for the second Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM) summit to be held in London in April 1998. THURSDAY, OCTOBER 2 LUXEMBOURG - EU telecoms ministers meet. No agenda yet available. FRIDAY, OCTOBER 3 LUXEMBOURG - EU internal market ministers hold informal meeting and structured dialogue with Central and East European countries (To October 4). No agenda yet available. MONDAY, OCTOBER 6 LUXEMBOURG - EU foreign ministers meet (To October 7). No agenda yet available. TUESDAY, OCTOBER 7 LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers meet. LUXEMBOURG - EU transport ministers meet and hold structured dialogue with Central and East European countries. No agenda yet available. BONN - Committee of the Regions holds seminar on "Cross-border and inter-regonal cooperation". Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155. MONDAY, OCTOBER 13 LUXEMBOURG - EU finance ministers meet. Speakers include: European Commission President Santer; Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt; European Commissioners Yves-Thibault de Silguy, Mario Monti, Monika Wulf-Mathies, Emma Bonino and Hans van den Broek; MEP Karl Von Wogau; Bank of England Governor Eddie George; Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes; Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo de Rato; World Trade Organisation Director General Renato Ruggiero; French Economy Minister Jean Arthuis; European Investment Bank President Brian Unwin. 291707 DED:BC-DIARY-LONGTERM =6 Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 6/6 - Nov 27-Dec 31) THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 27 BRUSSELS - EU internal market ministers meet.
